1.1: The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, the Sonne of God:
1.2: As it is written in the Prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
1.3: The voyce of him that cryeth in the wilderness is, Prepare the way of the Lord: make his paths straight.
1.4: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of amendment of life, for remission of sinnes.
1.5: And al ye countrey of Judea, and they of Hierusalem went out unto him, and were all baptized of him in the river Jordan, confessing their sinnes.
1.6: Now John was clothed with camels hear, and with a girdle of a skinne about his loynes: and he did eat Locusts and wild hony,
1.7: And preached, saying, A stronger then I cometh after me, whose shoes latchet I am not worthy to stoupe down, and unloose.
1.8: Trueth it is, I have baptized you with water: but he will baptize you with the holy Ghost.
1.9: And it came to pass in those dayes, that Jesus came from Nazareth, a citie of Galile, and was baptized of John in Jordan.
1.10: And assoone as he was come out of the water, John saw the heavens cloven in twain, and the holy Ghost descending upon him like a dove.
1.11: Then there was a voyce from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Sonne, in whom I am well pleased.
1.12: And immediatly the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.
1.13: And he was there in the wilderness fourtie daies, and was tempted of Satan: hee was also with the wild beastes, and the Angels ministred unto him.
1.14: Now after that John was committed to prison, Jesus came into Galile, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God,
1.15: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent and beleeue the Gospel.
1.16: And as he walked by the sea of Galile, he saw Simon, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, (for they were fishers.)
1.17: Then Jesus said unto them, Folow me, and I will make you to be fishers of men.
1.18: And straightway they forsook their nets, and folowed him.
1.19: And when hee had gone a litle further thence, he saw James the sonne of Zebedeus, and John his brother, as they were in the ship, mending their nets.
1.20: And anon hee called them: and they left their father Zebedeus in the shippe with his hired servants, and went their way after him.
1.21: So they entred into Capernaum, and straightway on the Sabbath day hee entred into the Synagogue, and taught.
1.22: And they were astonied at his doctrine, for he taught them as one that had authoritie, and not as the Scribes.
1.23: And there was in their Synagogue a man in whom was an vncleane spirit, and hee cried out,
1.24: Saying, Ah, what have we to do with thee, O Jesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroy us? I know thee what thou art, even that holy one of God.
1.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
1.26: And the vncleane spirit tare him, and cried with a loud voyce, and came out of him.
1.27: And they were all amased, so that they demaunded one of another, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for he commandeth even the fowl spirites with authoritie, and they obey him.
1.28: And immediatly his fame spred abroad throughout all the region bordering on Galile.
1.29: And assoone as they were come out of the Synagogue, they entred into the house of Symon and Andrew, with James and John.
1.30: And Symons wives mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they told him of her.
1.31: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up, and the fever forsook her by and by, and she ministred unto them.
1.32: And whe even was come, at what time the sunne setteth, they brought to him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.
1.33: And the whole citie was gathered together at the door.
1.34: And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases: and he cast out many devils, and suffred not the devils to say that they knew him.
1.35: And in the morning very early before day, Jesus arose and went out into a solitarie place, and there praied.
1.36: And Simon, and they that were with him, followed carefully after him.
1.37: And when they had found him, they sayde unto him, All men seek for thee.
1.38: Then he said unto them, Let us go into the next townes, that I may preach there also: for I came out for that purpose.
1.39: And hee preached in their Synagogues, throughout all Galile, and cast the devils out.
1.40: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeled down unto him, and said to him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
1.41: And Jesus had compassion, and put foorth his hand, and touched him, and said to him, I wil: be thou clean.
1.42: And assone as he had spoken, immediatly ye leprosie departed from him, and he was made clean.
1.43: And after he had give him a streight commandement, he sent him away forthwith,
1.44: And sayde unto him, See thou say nothing to any man, but get thee hence, and shew thy self to the Priest, and offer for thy clensing those things, which Moses commanded, for a testimoniall unto them.
1.45: But when he was departed, hee began to tel many things, and to publish the matter: so that Jesus could no more openly enter into the citie, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.

2.1: After a few dayes, hee entred into Capernaum again, and it was noysed that he was in the house.
2.2: And anon, many gathered together, in so much that the places about the door could not receive any more and he preached the word unto them.
2.3: And there came unto him, that brought one sick of the palsie, borne of four men.
2.4: And because they could not come neere unto him for the multitude, they vncouered ye roof of the house where hee was: and when they had broken it open, they let down the bed, wherein the sick of the palsie lay.
2.5: Now when Jesus saw their faith, he said to the sick of the palsie, Sonne, thy sinnes are forgiven thee.
2.6: And there were certain of the Scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
2.7: Why doeth this man speak such blasphemies? who can forgive sinnes, but God onely?
2.8: And immediatly when Jesus perceived in his spirit, that thus they reasoned with themselves, he sayde unto them, Why reason yee these things in your hearts?
2.9: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsie, Thy sinnes are forgiven thee? or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
2.10: But that ye may know, that the Sonne of man hath authoritie in earth to forgive sinnes, (he sayde unto the sick of the palsie.)
2.11: I say unto thee, Arise and take up thy bed, and get thee hence into thine own house.
2.12: And by and by he arose, and took up his bed, and went foorth before them all, in so much that they were all amased, and glorified God, saying, We never saw such a thing.
2.13: Then he went foorth again toward the sea, and all the people resorted unto him, and he taught them.
2.14: And as Jesus passed by, hee saw Levi the sonne of Alpheus sit at the receit of custom, and said unto him, Folowe me. And he arose and followed him.
2.15: And it came to pass, as Jesus sat at table in his house, many Publicanes and sinners sat at table also with Jesus, and his disciples: for there were many that followed him.
2.16: And when the Scribes and Pharises saw him eat with the Publicanes and sinners, they sayd unto his disciples, How is it, that hee eateth and drinketh with Publicanes and sinners?
2.17: Now when Jesus heard it, hee sayde unto them, The whole have no need of the Physicion, but the sick. I came not to call the righteous, but the sinners to repentance.
2.18: And the disciples of John, and the Pharises did fast, and came and said unto him, Why doe the disciples of John, and of the Pharises fast, and thy disciples fast not?
2.19: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the marriage chamber fast, whiles the bridegrome is with them? as long as they have the bridegrome with them, they cannot fast.
2.20: But the daies will come, when the bridegrome shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast in those daies.
2.21: Also no man soweth a piece of new cloth in an old garment: for els the new piece that filled it up, taketh away somewhat from the old, and the breach is worse.
2.22: Likewise, no man putteth new wine into old vessels: for els the new wine breaketh the vessels, and the wine runneth out, and the vessels are lost: but new wine must be put into new vessels.
2.23: And it came to pass as hee went through the corn on the Sabbath day, that his disciples, as they went on their way, began to pluck the eares of corn.
2.24: And the Pharises said unto him, Behold, why doe they on the Sabbath day, that which is not lawful?
2.25: And he said to them, Have yee never read what David did when he had need, and was an hungred, both he, and they that were with him?
2.26: How he went into the house of God, in the daies of Abiathar the hie Priest, and did eat the shew bread, which were not lawful to eat, but for the Priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
2.27: And hee sayde to them, The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
2.28: Wherefore the Sonne of man is Lord, even of the Sabbath.

3.1: And he entred again into ye Synagogue, and there was a man which had a withered had.
3.2: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
3.3: Then he said unto the man which had the withered hand, Arise: stand forth in the middes.
3.4: And he said to them, Is it lawful to doe a good deed on the Sabbath day, or to doe evil? to save the life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
3.5: Then hee looked round about on them angerly, mourning also for the hardness of their hearts, and said to the man, Stretch foorth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored, as whole as the other.
3.6: And the Pharises departed, and straightway gathered a council with the Herodians against him, that they might destroy him.
3.7: But Jesus avoided with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude followed him from Galile, and from Judea,
3.8: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and beyond Jordan: and they that dwelled about Tyrus and Sidon, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him in great number.
3.9: And he commanded his disciples, that a litle shippe should wait for him, because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.
3.10: For hee had healed many, in so much that they preassed upon him to touch him, as many as had plagues.
3.11: And when the vncleane spirits saw him, they fel down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Sonne of God.
3.12: And he sharply rebuked them, to the end they should not utter him.
3.13: Then hee went up into a mountain, and called unto him whom he would, and they came unto him.
3.14: And hee appoynted twelve that they should be with him, and that he might send them to preach,
3.15: And that they might have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils.
3.16: And the first was Simon, and hee named Simon, Peter,
3.17: Then James the sonne of Zebedeus, and John James brother (and surnamed them Boanerges, which is, the sonnes of thunder,)
3.18: And Andrew, and Philippe, and Bartlemew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James, the sonne of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Cananite,
3.19: And Judas Iscariot, who also betraied him, and they came home.
3.20: And the multitude assembled again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
3.21: And when his kinsfolkes heard of it, they went out to laie hold on him: for they sayde that he was beside himself.
3.22: And the Scribes which came down from Hierusalem, said, He hath Beelzebub, and through the prince of the devils he casteth out devils.
3.23: But he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan drive out Satan?
3.24: For if a kingdom bee deuided against it self, that kingdom can not stand.
3.25: Or if a house bee deuided against it self, that house can not continue.
3.26: So if Satan make insurrection against himself, and be deuided, hee can not endure but is at an end.
3.27: No man can enter into a strong mans house, and take away his goods, except hee first bind that strong man, and then spoyle his house.
3.28: Verely I say unto you, all sinnes shalbe forgiven unto the children of men, and blasphemies, wherewith they blaspheme:
3.29: But hee that blasphemeth against the holy Ghost, shall never have forgiveness, but is culpable of eternal damnation.
3.30: Because they said, Hee had an vncleane spirit.
3.31: Then came his brethren and mother, and stood without, and sent unto him, and called him.
3.32: And the people sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother, and thy brethren seek for thee without.
3.33: But hee answered them, saying, Who is my mother and my brethren?
3.34: And hee looked round about on them, which sat in compass about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren.
3.35: For whosoever doeth the will of God, he is my brother, and my sister, and mother.

4.1: And hee began again to teach by the sea side, and there gathered unto him a great multitude, so that hee entred into a shippe, and sat in the sea, and all the people was by the sea side on the land.
4.2: And he taught them many things in parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,
4.3: Hearken: Behold, there went out a sower to sow.
4.4: And it came to pass as he sowed, that some fell by the way side, and the foules of the heaven came, and deuoured it up.
4.5: And some fell on stonie ground, where it had not much earth, and by and by sprang up, because it had not depth of earth.
4.6: But assoone as ye Sunne was up, it was burnt up, and because it had not root, it withered away.
4.7: And some fell among the thornes, and the thornes grew up, and choked it, so that it gave no fruit.
4.8: Some again fell in good ground, and did yeelde fruit that sprong up, and grew, and it brought foorth, some thirtie fold, some sixtie fold, and some an hundreth fold.
4.9: Then he said unto them, He that hath eares to hear, let him hear.
4.10: And whe he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve, asked him of ye parable.
4.11: And he said unto them, To you it is given to know the mysterie of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all thinges bee done in parables,
4.12: That they seeing, may see, and not discern: and they hearing, may hear, and not understand, least at any time they should turn, and their sinnes should be forgiven them.
4.13: Again he said unto them, Perceive ye not this parable? how then should ye understand all other parables?
4.15: And these are they that receive the seed by the wayes side, in whom the word is sowen: but when they have heard it, Satan cometh immediatly, and taketh away the word that was sowen in their heartes.
4.16: And likewise they that receive the seed in stony ground, are they, which whe they have heard the word, straightwayes receive it with gladness.
4.17: Yet have they no root in themselves, and endure but a time: for when trouble and persecution ariseth for the word, immediatly they be offended.
4.18: Also they that receive the seed among the thornes, are such as hear the word:
4.19: But the cares of this world, and the deceitfulnes of riches, and the lustes of other things enter in, and choke the word, and it is unfruitful.
4.20: But they that have received seed in good ground, are they that hear the word, and receive it, and bring foorth fruit: one corn thirtie, another sixtie, and some an hundreth.
4.21: Also he said unto them, Cometh the candle in, to be put under a bushel, or under the bed, and not to be put on a candlestick?
4.22: For there is nothing hid, that shall not be opened: neither is there a secret, but that it shall come to light.
4.23: If any man have eares to hear, let him hear.
4.24: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear. With what measure ye mete, it shall be measured unto you: and unto you that hear, shall more be given.
4.25: For unto him that hath, shall it be given, and from him that hath not, shall be taken away, even that he hath.
4.26: Also he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed in the ground,
4.27: And should sleep, and rise up night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he not knowing how.
4.28: For the earth bringeth foorth fruit of it self, first the blade, then the eares, after that full corn in the eares.
4.29: And assoone as the fruit sheweth it self, anon hee putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
4.30: He said moreover, Whereunto shall wee liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?
4.31: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which when it is sowen in the earth, is the least of all seedes that be in the earth:
4.32: But after that it is sowen, it groweth up, and is greatest of all herbes, and beareth great branches, so that the foules of heaven may build under the shadow of it.
4.33: And with many such parables he preached the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.
4.34: And without parables spake hee nothing unto them: but he expounded all thinges to his disciples apart.
4.35: Now the same day when even was come, he said unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.
4.36: And they left the multitude, and took him as he was in the shippe, and there were also with him other little shippes.
4.37: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves dashed into the shippe, so that it was now full.
4.38: And he was in the stern asleep on a pillow: and they awoke him, and said to him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
4.39: And hee rose up, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, and be still. So the wind ceased, and it was a great calm.
4.40: Then he said unto them, Why are ye so fearefull? how is it that ye have no faith?
4.41: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, Who is this, that both the wind and sea obey him?

5.1: And they came over to the other side of the sea into the countrey of the Gadarens.
5.2: And when he was come out of the shippe, there met him incontinently out of the graves, a man which had an vncleane spirit:
5.3: Who had his abiding among the graves, and no man could bind him, no not with chaines:
5.4: Because that when hee was often bound with fetters and chaines, he plucked the chaines asunder, and brake the fetters in pieces, neither could any man tame him.
5.5: And alwayes both night and day he cryed in the mountaines, and in the graves, and strooke himself with stones.
5.6: And when he saw Jesus afarre off, he ranne, and worshipped him,
5.7: And cryed with a loud voyce, and said, What have I to doe with thee, Jesus the Sonne of the most high God? I will that thou swear to me by God, that thou torment me not.
5.8: (For hee said unto him, Come out of the man, thou vncleane spirit.)
5.9: And he asked him, What is thy name? and hee answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
5.10: And hee prayed him instantly, that hee would not send them away out of the countrey.
5.11: Now there was there in the mountaines a great heard of swine, feeding.
5.12: And all ye devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.
5.13: And incontinently Jesus gave them leave. Then the vncleane spirites went out, and entred into the swine, and the heard ranne headlong from the high bank into the sea, (and there were about two thousand swine) and they were choked up in the sea.
5.14: And the swineheards fled, and told it in the citie, and in the countrey, and they came out to see what it was that was done.
5.15: And they came to Jesus, and saw him that had been possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sit both clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
5.16: And they that saw it, told them, what was done to him that was possessed with the devil, and concerning the swine.
5.17: Then they began to pray him, that hee would depart from their coastes.
5.18: And when he was come into the shippe, he that had been possessed with the devil, prayed him that he might be with him.
5.19: Howbeit, Jesus would not suffer him, but said unto him, Goe thy way home to thy friendes, and shew them what great thinges the Lord hath done unto thee, and how hee hath had compassion on thee.
5.20: So he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis, what great things Jesus had done unto him: and all men did marueile.
5.21: And when Jesus was come over again by ship unto the other side, a great multitude gathered together to him, and he was neere unto the sea.
5.22: And behold, there came one of the rulers of the Synagogue, whose name was Jairus: and when he saw him, he fell down at his feet,
5.23: And besought him instantly, saying, My litle daughter lyeth at point of death: I pray thee that thou wouldest come and lay thine hands on her, that she may be healed, and live.
5.24: Then hee went with him, and a great multitude folowed him, and thronged him.
5.25: (And there was a certain woman, which was diseased with an issue of blood twelve yeeres,
5.26: And had suffred many things of many physicions, and had spent all that she had, and it auailed her nothing, but she became much worse.
5.27: When she had heard of Jesus, she came in the preasse behind, and touched his garment.
5.28: For she said, If I may but touch his clothes, I shalbe whole.
5.29: And straightway the course of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body, that she was healed of that plague.
5.30: And immediatly when Jesus did know in himself the vertue that went out of him, he turned him round about in the preasse, and said, Who hath touched my clothes?
5.31: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude throng thee, and sayest thou, Who did touch me?
5.32: And he looked round about, to see her that had done that.
5.33: And the woman feared and trembled: for she knew what was done in her, and she came and fell down before him, and told him the whole trueth.
5.34: And hee said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole: go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.)
5.35: While hee yet spake, there came from the same ruler of the Synagogues house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why diseasest thou the Master any further?
5.36: Assoone as Jesus heard that word spoken, he said unto the ruler of the Synagogue, Be not afraid: onely beleeue.
5.37: And he suffered no man to follow him save Peter and James, and John the brother of James.
5.38: So hee came unto the house of the ruler of the Synagogue, and saw the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
5.39: And he went in, and said unto them, Why make ye this trouble, and weep? the child is not dead, but sleepeth.
5.40: And they laught him to scorn: but hee put them all out, and took the father, and the mother of the child, and them that were with him, and entred in where the child lay,
5.41: And took the child by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi, which is by interpretation, Mayden, I say unto thee, arise.
5.42: And straightway the mayden arose, and walked: for she was of the age of twelve yeeres, and they were astonied out of measure.
5.43: And he charged them straitly that no man should know of it, and commanded to give her meat.

6.1: And he departed thence, and came into his own countrey, and his disciples followed him.
6.2: And when the Sabbath was come, he began to teach in the Synagogue, and many that heard him, were astonied, and sayd, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this that is given unto him, that even such great workes are done by his hands?
6.3: Is not this that carpenter Maries sonne, the brother of James and Joses, and of Juda and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended in him.
6.4: Then Jesus sayd unto them, A Prophet is not without honour, but in his own countrey, and among his own kindred, and in his own house.
6.5: And he could there doe no great workes, save that hee layd his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them,
6.6: And he marueiled at their vnbeliefe, and went about by ye townes on every side, teaching.
6.7: And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth two and two, and gave them power over vncleane spirits,
6.8: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff onely: neither scrip, neither bread, neither money in their girdles:
6.9: But that they should be shod with sandals, and that they should not put on two coates.
6.10: And he sayd unto them, Wheresoever ye shall enter into an house, there abide till ye depart thence.
6.11: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust that is under your feet, for a witnes unto them. Verely I say unto you, It shalbe easier for Sodom, or Gomorrha at the day of iudgement, then for that citie.
6.12: And they went out, and preached, that men should amend their lives.
6.13: And they cast out many devils: and they anointed many that were sick, with oyle, and healed them.
6.14: Then King Herod heard of him (for his name was made manifest) and sayd, John Baptist is risen again from the dead, and therefore great workes are wrought by him.
6.15: Other sayd, It is Elias, and some sayd, It is a Prophet, or as one of those Prophets.
6.16: So when Herod heard it, he said, It is John whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.
6.17: For Herod him self had sent forth, and had taken John, and bound him in prison for Herodias sake, which was his brother Philippes wife, because he had maried her.
6.18: For John sayd unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brothers wife.
6.19: Therefore Herodias layd wait against him, and would have killed him, but she could not:
6.20: For Herod feared John, knowing that hee was a just man, and an holy, and reverenced him, and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
6.21: But the time being convenient, when Herod on his birth day made a banket to his princes and captaines, and chief estates of Galile:
6.22: And the daughter of the same Herodias came in, and daunced, and pleased Herod, and them that sat at table together, the King sayd unto the mayde, Ask of me what thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
6.23: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, even unto the half of my kingdom.
6.24: So she went forth, and said to her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, John Baptists head.
6.25: Then she came in straightway with haste unto the King, and asked, saying, I would that thou shouldest give me even now in a charger the head of John Baptist.
6.26: Then the King was very sory: yet for his othes sake, and for their sakes which sat at table with him, he would not refuse her.
6.27: And immediatly the King sent the hangman, and gave charge that his head should be brought in. So he went and beheaded him in the prison,
6.28: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the maid, and the maid gave it to her mother.
6.29: And when his disciples heard it, they came and took up his body, and put it in a tomb.
6.30: And the Apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
6.31: And he sayd unto them, Come ye apart into the wildernes, and rest a while: for there were many comers and goers, that they had not leasure to eat.
6.32: So they went by ship out of the way into a desart place.
6.33: But the people saw them when they departed, and many knew him, and ran a foot thither out of all cities, and came thither before them, and assembled unto him.
6.34: Then Jesus went out, and saw a great multitude, and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep which had no shepheard: and he began to teach them many things.
6.35: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, saying, This is a desart place, and now the day is far passed.
6.36: Let them depart, that they may goe into the countrey and townes about, and buy them bread: for they have nothing to eat.
6.37: But he answered, and said unto them, Give yee them to eat. And they said unto him, Shall we goe, and buy two hundreth peny worth of bread, and give them to eat?
6.38: Then he sayde unto them, How many loaves have ye? goe and look. And when they knew it, they sayd, Five, and two fishes.
6.39: So he commanded them to make them all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
6.40: Then they sat down by rowes, by hundreds, and by fifties.
6.41: And he took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looked up to heaven, and gave thanks, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them, and the two fishes he deuided among them all.
6.42: So they did all eat, and were satisfied.
6.43: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
6.44: And they that had eaten, were about five thousand men.
6.45: And straightway he caused his disciples to goe into the ship, and to goe before unto the other side unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
6.46: Then assoone as he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.
6.47: And when even was come, the ship was in the mids of the sea, and he alone on the land.
6.48: And he saw them troubled in rowing, (for the wind was contrary unto them) and about the fourth watch of the night, hee came unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
6.49: And when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out.
6.50: For they all saw him, and were sore afrayd: but anon he talked with them, and said unto them, Be ye of good comfort: it is I, be not afrayd.
6.51: Then he went up unto them into the ship, and the wind ceased, and they were much more amased in them selves, and marueiled.
6.52: For they had not considered the matter of the loaves, because their hearts were hardened.
6.53: And they came over, and went into the land of Gennesaret, and arrived.
6.54: So when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
6.55: And ran about throughout all that region round about, and began to cary hither and thither in couches all that were sick, where they heard that he was.
6.56: And whithersoever he entred into townes, or cities, or villages, they laid their sick in the streetes, and prayed him that they might touch at the least the edge of his garment. And as many as touched him, were made whole.

7.1: Then gathered unto him the Pharises, and certain of the Scribes which came from Hierusalem.
7.2: And when they saw some of his disciples eat meat with common hands, (that is to say, unwashen) they complained.
7.3: (For the Pharises, and all the Iewes, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the Elders.
7.4: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not: and many other things there be, which they have taken upon them to observe, as the washing of cups, and pots, and of brasen vessels, and of beds.)
7.5: Then asked him the Pharises and Scribes, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the Elders, but eat meat with unwashen hands?
7.6: Then hee answered and sayd unto them, Surely Esay hath prophecied well of you, hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth mee with lippes, but their heart is far away from me.
7.7: But they worship me in vain, teaching for doctrines the commandements of men.
7.8: For ye lay the commandement of God apart, and observe the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and of cups, and many other such like things ye doe.
7.9: And he sayd unto them, Well, ye reiect the commandement of God, that ye may observe your own tradition.
7.10: For Moses sayd, Honour thy father and thy mother: and Whosoever shall speak evil of father or mother, let him die the death.
7.11: But yee say, If a man say to father or mother, Corban, that is, By the gift that is offered by mee, thou mayest have profit, hee shall be free.
7.12: So ye suffer him no more to doe any thing for his father, or his mother,
7.13: Making the word of God of none authoritie, by your tradition which ye have ordeined: and ye doe many such like things.
7.14: Then he called the whole multitude unto him, and sayd unto them, Hearken you all unto me, and understand.
7.15: There is nothing without a man, that can defile him, when it entreth into him: but the things which proceed out of him, are they which defile the man.
7.16: If any have eares to hear, let him hear.
7.17: And when hee came into an house, away from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
7.18: And he sayde unto them, What? are ye without understanding also? Doe ye not know that whatsoever thing from without entreth into a man, cannot defile him,
7.19: Because it entreth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught which is the purging of all meates?
7.20: Then he sayd, That which cometh out of man, that defileth man.
7.21: For from within, even out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughtes, adulteries, fornications, murthers,
7.22: Theftes, couetousnes, wickednes, deceit, vncleannes, a wicked eye, backbiting, pride, foolishness.
7.23: All these evil things come from within, and defile a man.
7.24: And from thence he rose, and went into the borders of Tyrus and Sidon, and entred into an house, and would that no man should have knowen: but he could not be hid.
7.25: For a certain woman, whose litle daughter had an vncleane spirit, heard of him, and came, and fell at his feet,
7.26: (And the woman was a Greek, a Syrophenissian by nation) and she besought him that he would cast out the devil out of her daughter.
7.27: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be fedde: for it is not good to take the childrens bread, and to cast it unto whelpes.
7.28: Then she answered, and said unto him, Trueth, Lord: yet in deed the whelpes eat under the table of the childrens crommes.
7.29: Then he said unto her, For this saying goe thy way: the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
7.30: And when she was come home to her house, she found the devil departed, and her daughter lying on the bed.
7.31: And hee departed again from the coastes of Tyrus and Sidon, and came unto the sea of Galile, through the middes of the coastes of Decapolis.
7.32: And they brought unto him one that was deaf and stambered in his speache, and prayed him to put his hand upon him.
7.33: Then hee took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers in his eares, and did spit, and touched his tongue.
7.34: And looking up to heaven, hee sighed, and said unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
7.35: And straightway his eares were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and hee spake plain.
7.36: And he commanded them, that they should tell no man: but how much soever hee forbad them, the more a great deal they published it,
7.37: And were beyond measure astonied, saying, Hee hath done all thinges well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the domme to speak.

8.1: In those dayes, when there was a very great multitude, and had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to him, and said unto them,
8.2: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now continued with mee three dayes, and have nothing to eat.
8.3: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they would faint by the way: for some of them came from far.
8.4: Then his disciples answered him, Whence can a man satisfie these with bread here in the wildernes?
8.5: And hee asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
8.6: Then he commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground: and hee took the seven loaves, and gave thankes, brake them, and gave to his disciples to set before them, and they did set them before the people.
8.7: They had also a few small fishes: and when he had given thankes, he commanded them also to be set before them.
8.8: So they did eat, and were sufficed, and they took up of the broken meat that was left, seven baskets full.
8.9: (And they that had eaten, were about four thousand) so he sent them away.
8.10: And anon he entred into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
8.11: And the Pharises came foorth, and began to dispute with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, and tempting him.
8.12: Then hee sighed deepely in his spirit, and said, Why doeth this generation seek a sign? Verely I say unto you, a sign shall not be given unto this generation.
8.13: So he left them, and went into the ship again, and departed to the other side.
8.14: And they had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the shippe with them, but one loaf.
8.15: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, and beware of the leaven of the Pharises, and of the leaven of Herod.
8.16: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is, because we have no bread.
8.17: And when Jesus knew it, he said unto them, Why reason you thus, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither vnderstande? have ye your hearts yet hardened?
8.18: Have yee eyes, and see not? and have yee eares, and hear not? and doe ye not remember?
8.19: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of broken meat took ye up? They said unto him, Twelve.
8.20: And when I brake seven among four thousand, how many baskets of the leauings of broken meat took ye up? And they said, Seven.
8.21: Then he said unto them, How is it that ye understand not?
8.22: And hee came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man unto him, and desired him to touch him.
8.23: Then he took the blind by the hand, and ledde him out of the town, and spat in his eyes, and put his handes upon him, and asked him, if he saw ought.
8.24: And he looked up, and said, I see men: for I see them walking like trees.
8.25: After that, he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look again. And hee was restored to his sight, and saw every man a far off clearely.
8.26: And hee sent him home to his house, saying, Neither goe into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.
8.27: And Jesus went out, and his disciples into the townes of Cesarea Philippi. And by the way hee asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom doe men say that I am?
8.28: And they answered, Some say, John Baptist: and some, Elias: and some, one of the Prophets.
8.29: And he said unto them, But whom say ye that I am? Then Peter answered, and said unto him, Thou art that Christ.
8.30: And he sharpely charged them, that concerning him they should tell no man.
8.31: Then hee began to teach them that the Sonne of man must suffer many things, and should be reproved of the Elders, and of the hie Priestes, and of the Scribes, and be slain, and within three dayes rise again.
8.32: And he spake that thing boldly. Then Peter took him aside, and began to rebuke him.
8.33: Then he turned back, and looked on his disciples, and rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou understandest not the things that are of God, but the things that are of men.
8.34: And hee called the people unto him with his disciples, and said unto them, Whosoever will follow me, let him forsake himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
8.35: For whosoever will save his life, shall lose it: but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the Gospels, he shall save it.
8.36: For what shall it profit a man, though he should win the whole world, if he lose his soul?
8.37: Or what exchange shall a man give for his soul?
8.38: For whosoever shall be ashamed of mee, and of my wordes among this adulterous and sinful generation, of him shall the Sonne of man be ashamed also, when he cometh in the glorie of his Father with the holy Angels.

9.1: And he said unto them, Verely I say unto you, that there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
9.2: And six dayes after, Jesus taketh unto him Peter, and James, and John, and carieth them up into an hie mountain out of the way alone, and his shape was changed before them.
9.3: And his rayment did shine, and was very white, as snow, so white as no fuller can make upon the earth.
9.4: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
9.5: Then Peter answered, and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: let us make also three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
9.6: Yet hee knew not what he said: for they were afraid.
9.7: And there was a cloud that shadowed them, and a voyce came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Sonne: hear him.
9.8: And suddenly they looked roud about, and saw no more any man save Jesus only with them.
9.9: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them, that they should tell no man what they had seen, save when the Sonne of man were risen from the dead again.
9.10: So they kept that matter to themselves, and demaunded one of another, what the rising from the dead again should mean?
9.11: Also they asked him, saying, Why say the Scribes, that Elias must first come?
9.12: And he answered, and said unto them, Elias verely shall first come, and restore all things: and as it is written of the Sonne of man, hee must suffer many things, and be set at nought.
9.13: But I say unto you, that Elias is come, (and they have done unto him whatsoever they would) as it is written of him.
9.14: And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the Scribes disputing with them.
9.15: And straightway all the people, when they beheld him, were amased, and ranne to him, and saluted him.
9.16: Then hee asked the Scribes, What dispute you among your selves?
9.17: And one of the companie answered, and said, Master, I have brought my sonne unto thee, which hath a dumme spirit:
9.18: And wheresoever he taketh him, he teareth him, and he fometh, and gnasheth his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples, that they should cast him out, and they could not.
9.19: Then he answered him, and said, O faithless generation, how long now shall I be with you! how long now shall I suffer you! Bring him unto me.
9.20: So they brought him unto him: and assoone as the spirit saw him, hee tare him, and hee fell down on the ground walowing and foming.
9.21: Then he asked his father, How long time is it since he hath bin thus? And he said, Of a child.
9.22: And oft times he casteth him into the fire, and into the water to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, help us, and have compassion upon us.
9.23: And Jesus said unto him, If thou canst beleeue it, al things are possible to him that beleeueth.
9.24: And straightway the father of the child crying with teares, said, Lord, I beleeue: help my vnbeliefe.
9.25: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the vncleane spirit, saying unto him, Thou domme and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
9.26: Then the spirit cried, and rent him sore, and came out, and he was as one dead, in so much that many said, He is dead.
9.27: But Jesus took his hand, and lift him up, and he arose.
9.28: And when hee was come into the house, his disciples asked him secretly, Why could not we cast him out?
9.29: And he said unto them, This kind can by no other meanes come foorth, but by prayer and fasting.
9.30: And they departed thence, and went together through Galile, and hee would not that any should have knowen it.
9.31: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Sonne of man shalbe delivered into the handes of men, and they shall kill him, but after that he is killed, he shall rise again the third day.
9.32: But they vnderstoode not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.
9.33: After, he came to Capernaum: and when he was in the house, he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among you by the way?
9.34: And they held their peace: for by the way they reasoned among themselves, who should bee the chiefest.
9.35: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and said to them, If any man desire to be first, the same shalbe last of all, and servant unto all.
9.36: And he took a litle child, and set him in the middes of them, and took him in his armes, and sayd unto them,
9.37: Whosoever shall receive one of such litle children in my Name, receiveth me: and whosoever receiveth mee, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.
9.38: Then John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils by thy Name, which followeth not us, and we forbad him, because he followeth us not.
9.39: But Jesus sayd, Forbid him not: for there is no man that can doe a miracle by my Name, that can lightly speak evil of me.
9.40: For whosoever is not against us, is on our part.
9.41: And whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink for my Names sake, because ye belong to Christ, verely I say unto you, he shall not lose his reward.
9.42: And whosoever shall offend one of these litle ones, that beleeue in me, it were better for him rather, that a milstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were cast into the sea.
9.43: Wherefore, if thine hand cause thee to offend, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life, maimed, then having two hands, to goe into hell, into the fire that never shalbe quenched,
9.44: Where their worm dyeth not, and the fire never goeth out.
9.45: Likewise, if thy foot cause thee to offend, cut it off: it is better for thee to go halt into life, then having two feet, to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shalbe quenched,
9.46: Where their worm dyeth not, and the fire never goeth out.
9.47: And if thine eye cause thee to offend, pluck it out: it is better for thee to goe into the kingdom of God with one eye, then having two eyes, to be cast into hell fire,
9.48: Where their worm dyeth not, and the fire never goeth out.
9.49: For every man shalbe salted with fire: and every sacrifice shalbe salted with salt.
9.50: Salt is good: but if the salt be vnsauerie, wherewith shall it be seasoned? have salt in your selves, and have peace one with another.

10.1: And he arose from thence, and went into the coastes of Judea by the far side of Jordan, and the people resorted unto him again, and as he was wont, he taught them again.
10.2: Then the Pharises came and asked him, if it were lawful for a man to put away his wife, and tempted him.
10.3: And he answered, and sayde unto them, What did Moses commaund you?
10.4: And they sayd, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
10.5: Then Jesus answered, and sayd unto them, For the hardness of your heart he wrote this precept unto you.
10.6: But at the beginning of the creation God made them male and female:
10.7: For this cause shall man leave his father and mother, and cleave unto his wife.
10.8: And they twain shalbe one flesh: so that they are no more twain, but one flesh.
10.9: Therefore, what God hath coupled together, let not man separate.
10.10: And in the house his disciples asked him again of that matter.
10.11: And he sayd unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife and marrie another, committeth adulterie against her.
10.12: And if a woman put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adulterie.
10.13: Then they brought litle children to him, that he should touch them, and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.
10.14: But when Jesus saw it, he was displeased, and said to them, Suffer the litle children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
10.15: Verely I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a litle child, he shall not enter therein.
10.16: And he took them up in his armes, and put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
10.17: And when hee was gone out on the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I doe, that I may possess eternal life?
10.18: Jesus sayde to him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, even God.
10.19: Thou knowest the comandements, Thou shalt not commit adulterie. Thou shalt not kill. Thou shalt not steal. Thou shalt not bear false witness. Thou shalt hurt no man. Honour thy father and mother.
10.20: Then he answered, and said to him, Master, all these things I have observed from my youth.
10.21: And Jesus looked upon him, and loved him, and sayde unto him, One thing is lacking unto thee. Go and sell all that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven, and come, follow me, and take up the cross.
10.22: But hee was sad at that saying, and went away sorowfull: for he had great possessions.
10.23: And Jesus looked round about, and sayd unto his disciples, How hardly doe they that have riches, enter into the kingdom of God!
10.24: And his disciples were afraid at his words. But Jesus answered again, and sayd unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches, to enter into the kingdom of God!
10.25: It is easier for a camel to goe through the eye of a needle, then for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
10.26: And they were much more astonied, saying with themselves, Who then can be saved?
10.27: But Jesus looked upon them, and sayd, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.
10.28: Then Peter began to say unto him, Loe, we have forsaken all, and have folowed thee.
10.29: Jesus answered, and sayd, Verely I say unto you, there is no man that hath forsaken house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands for my sake and the Gospels,
10.30: But he shall receive an hundred fold, now at this present, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands with persecutions, and in the world to come, eternal life.
10.31: But many that are first, shall be last, and the last, first.
10.32: And they were in the way going up to Hierusalem, and Jesus went before them and they were troubled, and as they followed, they were afraid, and Jesus took the twelve again, and began to tell them what things should come unto him,
10.33: Saying, Behold, we goe up to Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shall be delivered unto the hie Priests, and to the Scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him to the Gentiles.
10.34: And they shall mock him, and scourge him, and spit upon him, and kill him: but the third day he shall rise again.
10.35: Then James and John the sonnes of Zebedeus came unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest doe for us that we desire.
10.36: And he sayd unto them, What would ye I should doe for you?
10.37: And they said to him, Graunt unto us, that we may sit, one at thy right hand, and the other at thy left hand in thy glory.
10.38: But Jesus sayd unto them, Ye know not what ye ask. Can ye drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and be baptized with the baptism that I shall be baptized with?
10.39: And they said unto him, We can. But Jesus sayd unto them, Ye shall drink in deed of the cup that I shall drink of, and be baptized with the baptism wherewith I shalbe baptized:
10.40: But to sit at my right hand, and at my left, is not mine to give, but it shalbe given to them for whom it is prepared.
10.41: And when the ten heard that, they began to disdaine at James and John.
10.42: But Jesus called them unto him, and sayd to them, Ye know that they which are princes among the Gentiles, have domination over them, and they that be great among them, exercise authoritie over them.
10.43: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your servant.
10.44: And whosoever will be chief of you, shall be the servant of all.
10.45: For even the Sonne of man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life for the raunsome of many.
10.46: Then they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples, and a great multitude, Bartimeus the sonne of Timeus, a blind man, sat by the wayes side, begging.
10.47: And when hee heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry, and to say, Jesus the Sonne of David, have mercy on me.
10.48: And many rebuked him, because he should hold his peace: but hee cryed much more, O Sonne of David, have mercy on me.
10.49: Then Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called: and they called the blind, saying unto him, Be of good comfort: arise, he calleth thee.
10.50: So he threw away his cloke, and rose, and came to Jesus.
10.51: And Jesus answered, and said unto him, What wilt thou that I doe unto thee? And the blind sayd unto him, Lord, that I may receive sight.
10.52: Then Jesus sayde unto him, Goe thy way: thy fayth hath saved thee. And by and by, he received his sight, and folowed Jesus in the way.

11.1: And when they came neere to Hierusalem, to Bethphage and Bethania unto the mount of Olives, he sent forth two of his disciples,
11.2: And sayd unto them, Goe your wayes into that town that is over against you, and assoone as ye shall enter into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon never man sat: loose him, and bring him.
11.3: And if any man say unto you, Why doe ye this? Say that the Lord hath need of him, and straightway he will send him hither.
11.4: And they went their way, and found a colt tyed by the door without, in a place where two wayes met, and they loosed him.
11.5: Then certain of them, that stood there, sayd unto them, What doe ye loosing the colt?
11.6: And they sayde unto them, as Jesus had commanded them: So they let them goe.
11.7: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him, and he sat upon him.
11.8: And many spred their garments in the way: other cut down branches off the trees, and strawed them in the way.
11.9: And they that went before, and they that folowed, cryed, saying, Hosanna: blessed be hee that cometh in the Name of the Lord.
11.10: Blessed be the kingdom that cometh in the Name of the Lord of our father David: Hosanna, O thou which art in the highest heavens.
11.11: So Jesus entred into Hierusalem, and into the Temple: and when he had looked about on all things, and now it was evening, he went forth unto Bethania with the twelve.
11.12: And on the morowe when they were come out from Bethania, he was hungry.
11.13: And seeing a fig tree afarre off, that had leaves, he went to see if he might find any thing thereon: but when he came unto it, hee found nothing but leaves: for the time of figges was not yet.
11.14: Then Jesus answered, and sayd to it, Never man eat fruit of thee hereafter while the world standeth: and his disciples heard it.
11.15: And they came to Hierusalem, and Jesus went into the Temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the Temple, and overthrew the tables of the money changers, and the seates of them that sold doves.
11.16: Neither would hee suffer that any man should cary a vessell through the Temple.
11.17: And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, Mine house shalbe called the house of prayer unto all nations? but you have made it a denne of theeues.
11.18: And the Scribes and hie Priestes heard it, and sought how to destroy him: for they feared him, because the whole multitude was astonied at his doctrine.
11.19: But when even was come, Jesus went out of the citie.
11.20: And in the morning as they journeyed together, they saw the figge tree dried up from the rootes.
11.21: Then Peter remembred, and said unto him, Master, behold, the figge tree which thou cursedst, is withered.
11.22: And Jesus answered, and said unto them, Have the faith of God.
11.23: For verely I say unto you, that whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken away, and cast into the sea, and shall not wauer in his heart, but shall beleeue that those things which he saieth, shall come to pass, whatsoever he saieth, shall be done to him.
11.24: Therefore I say unto you, Whatsoever ye desire when ye pray, beleeue that ye shall have it, and it shalbe done unto you.
11.25: But when ye shall stand, and pray, forgive, if ye have any thing against any man, that your Father also which is in heaven, may forgive you your trespasses.
11.26: For if you will not forgive, your Father which is in heaven, will not pardon you your trespasses.
11.27: Then they came again to Hierusalem: and as he walked in the Temple, there came to him ye hie Priestes, and the Scribes, and the Elders,
11.28: And said unto him, By what authoritie doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authoritie, that thou shouldest doe these things?
11.29: Then Jesus answered, and said unto them, I will also ask of you a certain thing, and answer ye me, and I will tell you by what authoritie I do these things.
11.30: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.
11.31: And they thought with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did ye not beleeue him?
11.32: But if we say, Of men, we fear the people: for all men counted John, that he was a Prophet in deed.
11.33: Then they answered, and said unto Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answered, and said unto them, Neither will I tell you by what authoritie I doe these things.

12.1: And he began to speak unto them in parables, A certain man planted a vineyard, and copassed it with an hedge, and digged a pit for the winepress, and built a tower in it, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a strange countrey.
12.2: And at the time, he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive of the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.
12.3: But they took him, and beat him, and sent him away emptie.
12.4: And again he sent unto them another servant, and at him they cast stones, and brake his head, and sent him away shamefully handled.
12.5: And again he sent another, and him they slew, and many other, beating some, and killing some.
12.6: Yet had he one sonne, his dear beloved: him also he sent the last unto them, saying, They will reverence my sonne.
12.7: But ye husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir: come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shalbe ours.
12.8: So they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
12.9: What shall then the Lord of the vineyard doe? He will come and destroy these husbandmen, and give the vineyard to others.
12.10: Have ye not read so much as this Scripture? The stone which the builders did refuse, is made the head of the corner.
12.11: This was done of the Lord, and it is marueilous in our eyes.
12.12: Then they went about to take him, but they feared the people: for they perceived that he spake that parable against them: therefore they left him, and went their way.
12.13: And they sent unto him certain of the Pharises, and of ye Herodians that they might take him in his talk.
12.14: And when they came, they said unto him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou considerest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God truely, Is it lawful to give tribute to Cesar, or not?
12.15: Should we give it, or should we not give it? but he knew their hypocrisie, and said unto them, Why tempt ye me? Bring me a peny, that I may see it.
12.16: So they brought it, and he said unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? and they said unto him, Cesars.
12.17: Then Jesus answered, and said unto them, Give to Cesar the things that are Cesars, and to God, those that are Gods: and they marueiled at him.
12.18: Then came the Sadduces unto him, (which say, there is no resurrection) and they asked him, saying,
12.19: Master, Moses wrote unto us, If any mans brother die, and leave his wife, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and rayse up seed unto his brother.
12.20: There were seven brethren, and the first took a wife, and when he died, left no issue.
12.21: Then the second took her, and he died, neither did he yet leave issue, and the third likewise:
12.22: So those seven had her, and left no yssue: last of all the wife died also.
12.23: In the resurrection then, when they shall rise again, whose wife shall she be of them? for seven had her to wife.
12.24: Then Jesus answered, and said unto them, Are ye not therefore deceived, because ye know not the Scriptures, neither the power of God?
12.25: For when they shall rise again from the dead, neither men marry, nor wives are married, but are as the Angels which are in heaven.
12.26: And as touching the dead, that they shall rise again, have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
12.27: God is not ye God of the dead, but the God of the living. Ye are therefore greatly deceived.
12.28: Then came one of the Scribes that had heard them disputing together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, he asked him, Which is the first commandement of all?
12.29: Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandements is, Hear, Israel, The Lord our God is the onely Lord.
12.30: Thou shalt therefore love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandement.
12.31: And the second is like, that is, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thy self. There is none other commandement greater then these.
12.32: Then that Scribe said unto him, Well, Master, thou hast said the trueth, that there is one God, and that there is none but he,
12.33: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbour as himself, is more then all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.
12.34: Then when Jesus saw that he answered discreetely, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.
12.35: And Jesus answered and said teaching in the Temple, How say the Scribes that Christ is the sonne of David?
12.36: For David himself said by ye holy Ghost, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footestoole.
12.37: Then David himself calleth him Lord: by what meanes is he then his sonne? and much people heard him gladly.
12.38: Moreover he said unto them in his doctrine, Beware of the Scribes which love to goe in long robes, and love salutations in the markets,
12.39: And the chief seates in the Synagogues, and the first roumes at feastes,
12.40: Which deuoure widowes houses, even under a colour of long prayers. These shall receive the greater damnation.
12.41: And as Jesus sat over against the treasurie, he beheld how the people cast money into the treasurie, and many rich men cast in much.
12.42: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a quadrin.
12.43: Then he called unto him his disciples, and said unto them, Verely I say unto you, that this poor widow hath cast more in, then all they which have cast into the treasurie.
12.44: For they all did cast in of their superfluitie: but she of her pouertie did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

13.1: And as he went out of the Temple, one of his disciples said unto him, Master, see what maner stones, and what maner buildings are here.
13.2: Then Jesus answered and said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon a stone, that shall not be throwen down.
13.3: And as he sat on the mount of Olives, over against the Temple, Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew asked him secretly,
13.4: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shalbe the sign when all these things shalbe fulfilled?
13.5: And Jesus answered them, and began to say, Take heed lest any man deceive you.
13.6: For many shall come in my Name, saying, I am Christ, and shall deceive many.
13.7: Furthermore when ye shall hear, of wars, and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needes be: but the end shall not be yet.
13.8: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there shalbe earthquakes in divers quarters, and there shalbe famine and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorowes.
13.9: But take ye heed to your selves: for they shall deliver you up to the Councils, and to the Synagogues: ye shalbe beaten, and brought before rulers and Kings for my sake, for a testimoniall unto them.
13.10: And the Gospel must first be published among all nations.
13.11: But when they lead you, and deliver you up, be not careful before hand, neither studie what ye shall say: but what is given you at the same time, that speak: for it is not ye that speak, but the holy Ghost.
13.12: Yea, and the brother shall deliver the brother to death, and the father the sonne, and the children shall rise against their parents, and shall cause them to die.
13.13: And ye shall be hated of all men for my Names sake: but whosoever shall endure unto the end, he shalbe saved.
13.14: Moreover, when ye shall see the abomination of desolation (spoken of by Daniel the Prophet) set where it ought not, (let him that readeth, consider it) then let them that be in Judea, flee into the mountaines,
13.15: And let him that is upon the house, not come down into the house, neither enter therein, to fetch any thing out of his house.
13.16: And let him that is in the field, not turn back again to take his garment.
13.17: Then wo shalbe to the that are with child, and to them that give suck in those dayes.
13.18: Pray therefore that your flight be not in the winter.
13.19: For those dayes shalbe such tribulation, as was not from the beginning of ye creation which God created unto this time, neither shalbe.
13.20: And except that the Lord had shortened those dayes, no flesh should be saved: but for the elects sake, which he hath chosen, he hath shortened those dayes.
13.21: Then if any man say to you, Loe, here is Christ, or, lo, he is there, beleeue it not.
13.22: For false Christes shall rise, and false prophets, and shall shew signes and wonders, to deceive if it were possible the very elect.
13.23: But take ye heed: behold, I have shewed you all things before.
13.24: Moreover in those dayes, after that tribulation, the sunne shall wax dark, and ye moon shall not give her light,
13.25: And the starres of heaven shall fall: and the powers which are in heaven, shall shake.
13.26: And then shall they see the Sonne of man coming in ye cloudes, with great power and glory.
13.27: And he shall then send his Angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four windes, and from the utmost part of the earth to the utmost part of heaven.
13.28: Now learn a parable of the figge tree. When her bough is yet tender, and it bringeth foorth leaves, ye know that sommer is neere.
13.29: So in like maner, when ye see these things come to pass, know that the kingdom of God is neere, even at the doores.
13.30: Verely I say unto you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things be done.
13.31: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my woordes shall not pass away.
13.32: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the Angels which are in heaven, neither the Sonne himself, but the Father.
13.33: Take heed: watch, and praie: for yee know not when the time is.
13.34: For the Sonne of man is as a man going into a strange countrey, and leaveth his house, and giveth authoritie to his seruaunts, and to every man his woorke, and commandeth the porter to watch.
13.35: Watch ye therefore, (for ye know not whe ye master of the house will come, at eve, or at midnight, at the cock crowing, or in the dawning,)
13.36: Least if he come suddenly, he should find you sleeping.
13.37: And those things that I say unto you, I say unto all men, Watch.

14.1: And two daies after followed the feast of the Passeouer, and of vnleauened bread: and the hie Priests, and Scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
14.2: But they sayde, Not in the feast day, least there be any tumult among the people.
14.3: And when hee was in Bethania in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at table, there came a woman having a box of oyntment of spikenard, very costly, and she brake the box, and powred it on his head.
14.4: Therefore some disdained among themselves, and sayde, To what end is this waste of oyntment?
14.5: For it might have been sold for more then three hundreth pence, and been given unto the poor, and they murmured against her.
14.6: But Jesus said, Let her alone: why trouble yee her? she hath wrought a good work on me.
14.7: For yee have the poor with you alwaies, and when yee will yee may doe them good, but me yee shall not have alwaies.
14.8: She hath done that she could: she came afore hand to anoynt my body to the burying.
14.9: Verely I say unto you, wheresoever this Gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done, shalbe spoken of in remembrance of her.
14.10: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went away unto the hie Priestes, to betray him unto them.
14.11: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised that they would give him monie: therefore he sought how he might conveniently betraie him.
14.12: Now the first day of vnleauened bread, when they sacrificed the Passeouer, his disciples sayde unto him, Where wilt thou that we goe and prepare, that thou mayest eat the Passeouer?
14.13: Then hee sent foorth two of his disciples, and sayde unto them, Goe yee into the citie, and there shall a man meet you bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
14.14: And whithersoever he goeth in, say yee to the good man of the house, The Master sayeth, Where is the lodging where I shall eat the Passeouer with my disciples?
14.15: And he wil shew you an upper chamber which is large, trimmed and prepared: there make it readie for us.
14.16: So his disciples went foorth, and came to the citie, and found as he had said unto them, and made readie the Passeouer.
14.17: And at even he came with the twelve.
14.18: And as they sat at table and did eat, Jesus said, Verely I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me, which eateth with me.
14.19: Then they began to be sorowful and to say to him one by one, Is it I? And another, Is it I?
14.20: And he answered and sayde unto them, It is one of the twelve that dippeth with mee in the platter.
14.21: Truely the Sonne of man goeth his way, as it is written of him: but woe bee to that man, by whom the Sonne of man is betrayed: it had been good for that man, if hee had never been borne.
14.22: And as they did eat, Jesus took the bread, and when hee had given thankes, he brake it and gave it to them, and sayde, Take, eat, this is my bodie.
14.23: Also he took the cuppe, and when he had given thankes, gave it to them: and they all drank of it.
14.24: And he said unto them, This is my blood of that new Testament, which is shed for many.
14.25: Verely I say unto you, I wil drink no more of the fruit of ye vine until that day, that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
14.26: And when they had sung a Psalm, they went out to the mount of Olives.
14.27: Then Jesus said unto them, Al ye shall be offended by mee this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepheard, and the sheep shall be scattered.
14.28: But after that I am risen, I will goe into Galile before you.
14.29: And Peter said unto him, Although all men should be offended at thee, yet would not I.
14.30: Then Jesus said unto him, Verely I say unto thee, this day, even in this night, before the cock crow twise, thou shalt denie me thrise.
14.31: But he said more earnestly. If I should die with thee, I will not denie thee: likewise also said they all.
14.32: After, they came into a place named Gethsemane: then hee said to his disciples, Sit yee here, till I have praied.
14.33: And hee took with him Peter, and James, and John, and hee began to be troubled, and in great heaviness,
14.34: And said unto them, My soul is very heauie, even unto the death: tarie here, and watch.
14.35: So he went forward a litle, and fell down on the ground, and praied, that if it were possible, that hour might pass from him.
14.36: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee: take away this cup from me: neuertheles not that I will, but that thou wilt, be done.
14.37: Then hee came, and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest not thou watch one hour?
14.38: Watch ye, and pray, that ye enter not into tentation: the spirit in deed is ready, but the flesh is weak.
14.39: And again hee went away, and praied, and spake the same wordes.
14.40: And he returned, and found them a sleep again: for their eyes were heauie: neither knew they what they should answer him.
14.41: And he came the third time, and said unto them, Sleep henceforth, and take your rest: it is ynough: the hour is come: behold, the Sonne of man is delivered into the hands of sinners.
14.42: Rise up: let us go: loe, he that betraieth me, is at hand.
14.43: And immediatly while hee yet spake, came Judas that was one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swordes and staves from the hie Priests, and Scribes, and Elders.
14.44: And he that betraied him, had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, he it is: take him and lead him away safely.
14.45: And assoone as hee was come, hee went straightway to him, and said, Hail Master, and kissed him.
14.46: Then they laid their handes on him, and took him.
14.47: And one of them that stood by, drew out a sword, and smote a servant of the hie Priest, and cut off his ear.
14.48: And Jesus answered and said to them, Ye be come out as against a thief with swordes, and with staves, to take me.
14.49: I was daily with you teaching in the Temple, and yee took me not: but this is done that the Scriptures should be fulfilled.
14.50: Then they all forsook him, and fled.
14.51: And there followed him a certain yong man, clothed in linen upon his bare bodie, and the yong men caught him.
14.52: But he left his linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
14.53: So they led Jesus away to the hie Priest, and to him came together all the hie Priestes, and the Elders, and the Scribes.
14.54: And Peter folowed him afarre off, even into the hall of the hie Priest, and sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.
14.55: And the hie Priests, and all the Council sought for witness against Jesus, to put him to death, but found none.
14.56: For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.
14.57: Then there arose certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,
14.58: We heard him say, I will destroy this Temple made with hands, and within three daies I will build another, made without hands.
14.59: But their witness yet agreed not together.
14.60: Then the hie Priest stood up amongst them, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is the matter that these bear witness against thee?
14.61: But hee held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the hie Priest asked him, and sayde unto him, Art thou that Christ the Sonne of the Blessed?
14.62: And Jesus said, I am he, and yee shall see the Sonne of man sitte at the right hand of the power of God, and come in the clouds of heaven.
14.63: Then the hie Priest rent his clothes, and sayd, What have we any more need of witnesses?
14.64: Ye have heard the blasphemie: what think yee? And they all condemned him to be worthie of death.
14.65: And some began to spit at him, and to cover his face, and to beat him with fists, and to say unto him, Prophesie. And the sergeants smote him with their roddes.
14.66: And as Peter was beneath in the hal, there came one of the maides of the hie Priest.
14.67: And when she saw Peter warming him self, she looked on him, and sayde, Thou wast also with Jesus of Nazareth.
14.68: But he denied it, saying, I know him not, neither wot I what thou saiest. Then he went out into the porch, and the cock crew.
14.69: Then a maid saw him again, and bega to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
14.70: But hee denied it again: and anon after, they that stood by, sayde again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art of Galile, and thy speach is like.
14.71: And he began to curse, and swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
14.72: Then the second time the cock crew, and Peter remembred the woorde that Jesus had said unto him, Before the cock crow twise, thou shalt denie me thrise, and waying that with himself, he wept.

15.1: And anon in the dawning, the hie Priestes held a Council with the Elders, and the Scribes, and the whole Council, and bound Jesus, and led him away, and delivered him to Pilate.
15.2: Then Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Iewes? And hee answered, and sayde unto him, Thou sayest it.
15.3: And the hie Priestes accused him of many things.
15.4: Wherefore Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they witness against thee.
15.5: But Jesus answered no more at all, so that Pilate marueiled.
15.6: Now at the feast, Pilate did deliver a prisoner unto them, whomesoeuer they would desire.
15.7: Then there was one named Barabbas, which was bound with his fellowes, that had made insurrection, who in the insurrection had committed murder.
15.8: And the people cried aloud, and began to desire that he would doe as he had ever done unto them.
15.9: Then Pilate answered them, and said, Will ye that I let loose unto you the King of ye Iewes?
15.10: For he knew that the hie Priestes had delivered him of enuie.
15.11: But the high Priestes had moved the people to desire that he would rather deliver Barabbas unto them.
15.12: And Pilate answered, and said again unto them, What will ye then that I doe with him, whom ye call the King of the Iewes?
15.13: And they cried again, Crucifie him.
15.14: Then Pilate said unto them, But what evil hath he done? And they cryed the more fervently, Crucifie him.
15.15: So Pilate willing to content the people, loosed them Barabbas, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, that he might be crucified.
15.16: Then the souldiers led him away into the hall, which is the common hall, and called together the whole band,
15.17: And clad him with purple, and platted a crown of thornes, and put it about his head,
15.18: And began to salute him, saying, Hail, King of the Iewes.
15.19: And they smote him on the head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowed the knees, and did him reverence.
15.20: And whe they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucifie him.
15.21: And they compelled one that passed by, called Simon of Cyrene (which came out of the countrey, and was father of Alexander and Rufus) to bear his cross.
15.22: And they brought him to a place named Golgotha, which is by interpretation, the place of dead mens skulles.
15.23: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.
15.24: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots for them, what every man should have.
15.25: And it was the third hour, when they crucified him.
15.26: And ye title of his cause was written above, THAT KING OF THE JEWES.
15.27: They crucified also with him two theeues, the one on ye right hand, and the other on his left.
15.28: Thus the Scripture was fulfilled, which sayth, And he was counted among the wicked.
15.29: And they that went by, railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Hey, thou that destroyest the Temple, and buildest it in three dayes,
15.30: Save thy self, and come down from the cross.
15.31: Likewise also even the hie Priests mocking, said among themselves with the Scribes, He saved other men, himself he cannot save.
15.32: Let Christ the King of Israel now come down from the cross, that we may see, and beleeue. They also that were crucified with him, reviled him.
15.33: Now when the sixt hour was come, darkenesse arose over all the land until the ninth hour.
